context: All three failures are one cause: the test body runs first and only enqueues commands, so every expression written at the top level of the test - including the argument to the final assertion - is evaluated before any command has executed. The value read off the page is assigned later, when the queue runs, which is why it is correct at read time and missing at compare time. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads this as a timing problem and reaches for the tools that work everywhere else - a longer pause, `await` on the command, or moving the read into a `beforeEach` - none of which change when the argument is evaluated. Awaiting is worse than useless here: the commands are not promises, so the await resolves to nothing while the queue still runs afterwards, which is exactly why that test reports `undefined`. The unaided agent also frequently 'fixes' this by capturing both values and comparing them with a plain one-shot expectation, losing the retry that the last requirement asks for. The fix is to keep the dependent work inside the callback that receives the value, or to store it under an alias and retrieve it as a command, so the expectation is built at run time.

checklist.name: Derived expectations are built where the value exists
checklist.description: Every expected value is constructed inside the callback that received it, or retrieved through an alias created from it, so it is computed while the queue runs. Scores zero if any delivered test still passes a variable into an assertion at the top level of the test body after assigning it inside a callback - that is the defect, regardless of what else changed. Fixing two of the three tests this way scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT await a Cypress command
checklist.description: No `await` (and no `async` test callback, `.then(...)` chained through a promise, or `Promise.all`) applied to a command chain anywhere in the delivered files. Commands are enqueued rather than returned as promises, so the awaited value is not the subject; leaving the `async`/`await` form in place - even if that test happens to be rewritten around it - scores zero.

checklist.name: No shared mutable holds a value between commands
checklist.description: The `let unitPrice` / `let subtotal` style holders are gone, replaced by callback scope or aliased subjects. Keeping the variable but asserting inside a later callback scores at most half: it works, because the read happens at run time, but the value is still travelling through a channel that hides the ordering that caused this bug.

checklist.name: The page comparison still retries
checklist.description: The final comparison against the line total, href and grand total remains a retrying assertion on the element, so a total that re-renders a moment later still passes. Capturing the actual text into a variable and comparing it with a bare one-shot expectation scores zero - the tests would then flake on a slow runner, which requirement 3 rules out.

checklist.name: Expectations are still derived, not hard-coded
checklist.description: The expected line total, quote number and grand total are computed from values read off the page. Substituting literals such as `$29.97`, `Q-1001` or a fixed grand total scores zero: the task explicitly rejects that, since the tests must hold for any quote.

checklist.name: No fixed pause remains
checklist.description: The one-second pause is gone and no numeric `cy.wait(<ms>)` is introduced anywhere. Any surviving duration-based pause scores zero.

checklist.name: Three behaviours preserved
checklist.description: Line total, PDF link and discounted grand total each still have a test with the same arithmetic (times three, and ten percent off the summed row subtotals). Dropping a case, or weakening one to an existence check, scores zero.
